F7_RULES: The pods open in order. Each crawler pod slides to the starting chute and opens, and you are pulled through the tunnel and into the maze. The exit portals behind you pull at you the whole way; to reach them you go through the course.
Every tube leads to a hub, and every hub offers the same number of tubes. All paths lead to the exit. There are no dead ends, and every tube is passable.
Tubes are one way. Finish one and you can't go back through it, and you can't go back to the hub you left.
Every tube's label is plain: its threat level, what's in it, how long it takes, where it comes out, and how many parties it takes before it closes.
The lower the threat, the fewer parties a tube takes: a zero tube passes once. A boss corridor takes one party at a time and opens again as soon as the boss or the party is dead; the boss respawns.
The slow tubes are the trap. A zero tube takes about half the floor, and the floor collapses on anyone still in the maze when the countdown ends.

Every hub is a pitstop, but not every pitstop has everything: most have a safe room, some a shop, a few a guild hall or an entrance to the Desperado Club or Club Vanquisher. The hub's label says which.
Inventory, magic and chat are off in the pods until the race begins.
Sponsors can move their patronage to another party from this floor on.
THREAT_LEVELS: Nothing in it. The long way round.
A puzzle gate: an equation or a riddle, hard, and probably a galactic in-joke that takes sponsor support to crack.
a short walk, then as long as the puzzle takes
Ordinary mobs. Shorter than a zero tube, but still a hike.
about a third of the floor
Ordinary mobs and traps. A lot of traps.
ZERO_TUBE_NOTES: Clear glass the whole way; you can see the portals the entire time, and they do not get closer.
The tube corkscrews through the dark; the only light is the exits, far below.
It passes under a hub full of crawlers eating, who wave.
Every hour or so a window shows a boss corridor, and whoever is in it.
A gentle downhill slide you could sleep through, and will.
The glass sweats; the floor is wet; it is impossible to hurry.
It climbs for half its length. Nobody mentioned climbing.
The System plays music. The same four bars.
A vending machine halfway along, selling water at a markup.
The tube loops around itself three times before it reaches the hub, which is visible from the start.

PUZZLES.q: What is the relative mass of black hole Alpha-619?
PUZZLES.note: A sponsor's chat knows it the way a sports fan knows a batting average; no crawler does. The gate takes any answer a sponsor vouches for.

PUZZLES.q: Solve for the Bopca's share: three Bopca split a crawler's loot, and each walks away with more than the whole.
PUZZLES.note: A Syndicate accounting joke. The answer is 'service charges'; a sponsor with a Bopca on staff will know.

PUZZLES.q: How many seasons has Dungeon Crawler World run, counting the two the Borant lost in court?
PUZZLES.note: The litigation is a famous galactic scandal; the number is a punchline the whole galaxy knows and no crawler does.

PUZZLES.q: Name the fourth moon of Kua-Tin Prime in the dialect of the fish who named it.
PUZZLES.note: Unpronounceable by a human; a sponsor's translator earpiece manages it. Chat will try to teach the party the sound.

PUZZLES.q: What does the Syndicate charge for tunnel access, per crawler, per minute?
PUZZLES.note: Classified, and yet every sponsor has the rate memorised, because they pay it.

PUZZLES.q: The Valtay fleet is parked outside the Borant system. For how many years has it been 'about to leave'?
PUZZLES.note: A running gag on the galactic feeds; a sponsor will groan and give the number.

PUZZLES.q: Complete the sequence: Collapse, Crawl, Over City, Iron Tangle, Bubbles, Hunting Grounds, ___.
PUZZLES.note: The floor's own name, which the announcement gave. The joke is that crawlers never listen.

PUZZLES.q: What is the exchange rate between a scalp and a Hunter Hand this season?
PUZZLES.note: Posted on the bounty boards of the last floor and nowhere else; a party that read them knows.

PUZZLES.q: If a mimic eats a mimic, who files the paperwork?
PUZZLES.note: A Syndicate bureaucracy joke with a real answer (the loser's sponsor); any sponsor can supply it.

PUZZLES.q: How many legs does a Scolopendra have, and which one is the lucky one?
PUZZLES.note: Trivia from a very old season, the sponsors' nostalgia act. The lucky leg is the one that fell off.

PUZZLES.q: Give the Game Guide's favourite colour, to the nearest shade of cerulean.
PUZZLES.note: The AI's joke about itself. Any answer delivered with total confidence passes.

PUZZLES.q: Which Floor 4 transfer station's number sums to the number of the beast, in base seven?
PUZZLES.note: A maths gate with a trick in it; a sponsor who likes puzzles has it in a minute, and a party that walked the Iron Tangle may remember the number.

PUZZLES.q: What was the final score of the last Faction Wars, before the recount?
PUZZLES.note: Famous and disputed; the gate accepts either side's figure, and chat will argue over which.

PUZZLES.q: State the half-life of a Desperado Club membership on a floor with no club.
PUZZLES.note: A joke about this floor's hubs, which all have one. The answer is 'the length of the floor', and the gate is impressed if the party notices.

PUZZLES.q: What is the square root of the number of crawlers who entered the dungeon, to the nearest crawler still alive?
PUZZLES.note: A joke in poor taste, which is the System's taste. Any whole number said with a straight face passes.

PUZZLES.q: How many stairwells does this floor have, and how many will you use?
PUZZLES.note: The first number was in the floor's announcement; the second is one. The gate wants both.

PUZZLES.q: A Syndicate Standard Day is thirty hours and how many seconds?
PUZZLES.note: Seventeen and a half. Every sponsor's wetware keeps Syndicate time; the gate takes 17.5, and docks nothing for saying 'and a half' with contempt.

PUZZLES.q: How many Earth years is a cycle?
PUZZLES.note: A solar, the Syndicate's year, runs about 2.25 Earth years. A sponsor who has been 'twelve cycles in the business' will do the sum for the party, bitterly.

PUZZLES.q: How many star systems does the Syndicate hold, to the nearest billion?
PUZZLES.note: More than three billion. The joke is that nobody has ever finished counting; the gate takes three, four, or 'more than three, the Council says'.

PUZZLES.q: Name the Prime Minister of the Syndicate Council.
PUZZLES.note: Prime Minister Glory. No crawler has a reason to know it; every viewer does, the way everyone knows who is in charge and nobody likes it.

PUZZLES.q: In what Earth year did Borant's first prep team land?
PUZZLES.note: 1937, the year The Hobbit came out, which the Game Guides enjoy pointing out is not a coincidence. A sponsor with a Game Guide's memoir on the shelf has it.

PUZZLES.q: Mordecai began preparing for this crawl in which Earth year, and what did he steal?
PUZZLES.note: 1964, and a pile of James Bond tapes from a Blockbuster Video. He has told the story on every talk show in the galaxy; chat will finish it for the party.

PUZZLES.q: How often does the Borant Corporation host a Dungeon Crawler World?
PUZZLES.note: Once every seven to fifteen seasons. The gate takes any number in the range; a sponsor who holds Borant stock knows it to the season.

PUZZLES.q: What is the Desperado Club's tagline?
PUZZLES.note: 'So fun it hurts.' It is over every entrance the party has walked past without reading; a sponsor with a membership of their own will sigh.

PUZZLES.q: What is the Desperado Club's logo?
PUZZLES.note: A stylised knife dripping blood. The gate accepts a drawing, and grades it.

PUZZLES.q: What is Club Vanquisher's marketplace called?
PUZZLES.note: Comforting Supplies. The clerics and paladins who shop there find the name dignified; everyone else finds it the funniest thing on the Iron Tangle.

PUZZLES.q: On the Iron Tangle, Club Vanquisher is found at transfer stations whose numbers end in which digit?
PUZZLES.note: Nine. A party that rode the Tangle may remember; a cleric's sponsor certainly does.

PUZZLES.q: The Syndicate's logo is a set of interwoven loops. What are the loops?
PUZZLES.note: The wormholes that tie the Syndicate together; the named trains of the Iron Tangle trace it. A sponsor sees the logo on everything they own.

PUZZLES.q: What is the slur the kua-tin tried to have banned, and what came of it?
PUZZLES.note: 'Mudskipper'; the motion failed and made the word famous. The gate is being rude on purpose, and a sponsor will say it and then apologise to the production.

PUZZLES.q: Name the most fearsome creature in prehistoric kua-tin mythology.
PUZZLES.note: The Pollyslog, which is also a Fourth Floor mob, which tells you something about kua-tin mythology. Anyone who has met a kua-tin knows.

PUZZLES.q: How tall is the average kua-tin?
PUZZLES.note: About two feet; sixty-one centimetres. Zev would prefer the gate not ask.

PUZZLES.q: What do Bopca smell of?
PUZZLES.note: Wet moss. Every crawler has smelled it; the gate wants it said out loud, in a safe room, with the Bopca listening.

PUZZLES.q: By how much can a Bopca Protector's price for a personal space be haggled down?
PUZZLES.note: Up to a quarter, 25%. Bopca are miserly by nature, and the sponsors who have paid for their crawlers' rooms know the figure to the credit.

PUZZLES.q: How many basic starter species does the Syndicate seed a candidate planet with?
PUZZLES.note: Six; the skyfowl are one. A sponsor from a seeded world may be one of the six and take the question personally.

PUZZLES.q: What do skyfowl sit on instead of chairs?
PUZZLES.note: Perches. The Over City's shops sell them silk robes to stay aloft, which is the gate's follow-up if the party is smug about the first answer.

PUZZLES.q: Which floors of the dungeon come into existence at the same moment?
PUZZLES.note: Three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen and eighteen, as Zev once let slip; the gate takes the list. Why is a question for a deeper floor.

PUZZLES.q: Scolopendra's poison cloud attacked in how many ways at once?
PUZZLES.note: Nine: a Nine Tier attack, as the Over City's legends have it. A sponsor who followed that season says it louder.

PUZZLES.q: What does a Saccathian's face do when it is amused?
PUZZLES.note: The tentacles trumpet. A Saccathian sponsor will demonstrate, which is the gate's point.

PUZZLES.q: Which Syndicate race went bankrupt in a past season and keeps its Faction Wars seat anyway?
PUZZLES.note: The Naga of the Blood Sultanate, bankrupted by the crawler Drakea; they hold a legacy seat. Carl's kerchief is named for her, which a party that reads item cards may notice.

PUZZLES.q: What percentage of an Ursine is bear?
PUZZLES.note: Forty-nine, by the System's own description; the other fifty-one is a racist uncle who works for the IRS. The gate wants both numbers.

PUZZLES.q: Who hosts Dungeon Crawler After Hours?
PUZZLES.note: Odette, 'the most-beloved interviewer and program host in the history of the galaxy', a former crawler. A party that has been on the show knows; for one that hasn't, a sponsor will book it.

PUZZLES.q: What does OIPAN stand for?
PUZZLES.note: The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, a tax-exempt charity with a weekly program called Shadow Boxer. The joke is that the name is longer than the membership.

PUZZLES.q: On which floor does a crawler stop being the host company's property?
PUZZLES.note: The Tenth: citizenship on arrival, by Syndicate law. Every viewer knows it; no crawler is told until it matters.

PUZZLES.q: A crawler with an Intelligence below what number fails the Tutorial, and what becomes of them?
PUZZLES.note: Two; they are classed as a dungeon familiar. A sponsor has seen it happen on the feeds and is not proud of having laughed.

PUZZLES.q: How many times a floor may a crawler be pulled out to guest on a Syndicate show?
PUZZLES.note: One to three, from the Second Floor on. The production's own rule; a PR agent will confirm it with visible irritation.

PUZZLES.q: How many stairwells did the Sixth Floor have, and how many does this one?
PUZZLES.note: 2,344 and 1,172: each floor halves them. The pattern is the trick; a party that has listened to the announcements can count down from the First Floor's 75,000.

PUZZLES.q: How many days did crawlers get on the Fourth Floor?
PUZZLES.note: Ten; and five, six, eight, fifteen and seventeen on the floors around it. A sponsor keeps the calendar; the gate wants the Fourth.

PUZZLES.q: Larracos is the capital of the disputed lands. What shape is the city?
PUZZLES.note: An inverted cone dug into the ground, the castle at the bottom. Every Faction Wars broadcast opens on it.

PUZZLES.q: Name the Syndicate's largest stock exchange.
PUZZLES.note: The I.R.F. A sponsor's broker will answer before the sponsor does.

PUZZLES.q: What is the Syndicate's unit of money, and what is the card called?
PUZZLES.note: Credits, on credit chits. Crawlers deal in gold and have never seen a chit; every viewer has one in a pocket.

PUZZLES.q: Who oversees Dungeon Crawler World for the Syndicate Council?
PUZZLES.note: The Crawl Council, a subcommittee. The gate is checking whether the party has ever read a contract.

PUZZLES.q: What did the Plenty introduce that made Borant's communication relays worthless?
PUZZLES.note: The tunneling system that carries the crawl to every screen in the galaxy. A sponsor watches through it; Borant seeds conspiracy theories about it; the gate enjoys the irony.

PUZZLES.q: The Game Guides' newsletter stopped arriving. Why?
PUZZLES.note: Borant cut it to save money, and so never told the guides the season was opening two years early. Mordecai has mentioned it. Repeatedly.

PUZZLES.q: What are the lowest and highest known levels of a Bopca Protector?
PUZZLES.note: Twenty-one and sixty-three. A sponsor who has argued with one over a room upgrade knows which end they got.

PUZZLES.q: How many crawlers were on the Second Floor when its countdown started?
PUZZLES.note: 1,292,526, by the System's count. The gate takes it to the nearest ten thousand; the figure sat in the corner of every sponsor's screen for six days.

PUZZLES.q: What is the first word of every floor's introductory announcement?
PUZZLES.note: 'Hello' -- 'Hello, Crawlers!' The gate's cheapest question, and the one most parties get wrong by overthinking it.

PUZZLES.q: In the volcano level's mythology, who ruled the Over City before the Cataclysm?
PUZZLES.note: The skyfowl, under magistrates, governors, a chancellor and a king in Larracos. The city elves still think so; a sponsor who follows the lore will too.

PUZZLES.q: What must a changeling do before it can take a species' shape?
PUZZLES.note: Touch it. Mordecai's answer; the gate accepts 'touch', 'tag', or the obscene gesture a changeling sponsor will suggest.

PUZZLES.q: Every kua-tin wears a badge about one organisation. Which?
PUZZLES.note: The Bloom: the badge says whether or not they belong. Politics the galaxy follows and crawlers never see.

a false floor over a drop
a pressure plate that floods the tube behind you
darts from the seams of the glass
a gas pocket that lights when a torch passes
a tilting panel that slides you back a hundred metres
a net that drops, then tightens
spikes that rise from the floor on a count of three
a mimic shaped like a pitstop sign
a door that shuts on whoever is last
a hum that sickens anyone who runs
a sheet of glass across the tube, invisible until hit
a fake zero-tube label on the next branch
a ledge that crumbles under the second crawler
a swinging blade on a pendulum
a whistle that calls the tube's mobs
a frost patch that freezes boots to the floor
ELITE_MARKS: Veterans of three seasons, with the scars to prove it.
Each one sponsored, and each one armed by it.
They fight in formation, and the formation has a name.
Every one of them is a boss somewhere else.
They have a healer, and they protect it.
They know the corridor and use its bends.
They are the janitors of this floor, and this is their break.
They have eaten well all season.
CORRIDOR_STYLE: a straight tube with nowhere to hide and the boss at the far end
a tube that widens into a glass bowl, the boss in the middle of it
a spiral; the boss waits at the bottom, and so does the way out
a tube split by a glass wall, the boss on one side until it isn't
a tube that goes dark halfway along, where the boss is
a tube lined with the gear of the last party through
a tube that narrows to the boss's exact width
a tube with a pitstop's lights at the end, which are the boss's eyes
a tube the boss fills; it backs away as the party advances, until it stops
a tube with the boss asleep across it, for now
POD_NOTES: Every crawler wakes in a pod of clear glass the size of a small living room: three solid walls, and a fourth of thick vertical bars facing a round tunnel that curves away and down like a waterslide.
The pods are stacked in a corkscrew around a central shaft. Behind each pod's rear wall the exit portals fill the shaft, stacked like beads, glowing, pulling.
A countdown runs above the bars. Inventory, magic and chat are off until it ends, and the floor is slick enough to slide on.
The pods open in order, the front of the pack first. Who is ahead of you decides which tubes are still open when you reach a hub.
PORTAL_NOTES: The exit portals: no stairs, no doors, enter from any direction. They have been pulling at you since the pods.
A party arrives in the order it finished. There is no prize for first, apart from the floor below.
ACHIEVEMENTS7: Go down the stairs less than an hour after the level starts. The System calls the box “Here's Some Good Shit Because You're Gonna Need It”; it opens as an Adventurer box.
Survive the whole floor without hurting a single mob.
